policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'their lamps' renders either the reflexive heauton or the plain auton identically; the only note is an alternative_rendering about 'torches' and does not touch the pronoun.
hypantesin and apantesin are both 'to meet the bridegroom'; the ASV wording cannot separate the two compounds.
Pure word order within 'five of them were foolish'; English fixes the order independently of the Greek sequence.
ASV names the foolish first and the wise second ('five of them were foolish, and five were wise'), matching morai kai pente phronimoi; the alternative reverses the two clauses.
ASV opens the verse with the causal 'For the foolish...', rendering hai gar; the relative haitines would have continued the previous sentence with 'who/which'.
ASV 'in their vessels' can render the articular angeiois as a possessive, English idiom for the Greek article, as readily as an explicit auton; the plus is not distinguished.
'with their lamps' renders heauton and auton alike; the 'torches' note concerns the noun, not the pronoun.
ASV has the bare exclamation 'Behold, the bridegroom!' with no verb; the added erchetai would have produced 'the bridegroom cometh'.
ASV renders the object pronoun, 'Come ye forth to meet him'; the reading that omits autou would leave 'go forth to meet' without 'him'.
'trimmed their lamps' is the same English for heauton and auton.
ASV 'there will not be enough' renders the emphatic ou me and the simple ouk with the same negation; English carries no emphatic form to distinguish them.

ASV continues asyndetically after the colon, 'go ye rather to them that sell'; the added de would have surfaced as 'but go ye rather', which this literal revision renders elsewhere in the verse ('But the wise answered').
ASV ends the verse at 'nor the hour'; the longer reading's clause 'wherein the Son of man cometh' is wholly absent from the English.
ASV begins 'Straightway he that received...' with no connective; the added de would have given 'And/But he that received', and the base's eutheos is what 'Straightway' renders.

ASV 'made other five talents' follows 'traded with them', where 'made' is an idiomatic English rendering of kerdaino (gained a profit) as well as the literal poieo; the verb choice does not settle the reading.
ASV 'other five talents' supplies the noun the elliptical alla pente leaves implicit, which English requires here; the printed 'talents' does not by itself witness the Greek plus.
ASV's single 'also' in 'he also that received the two' could render this kai, the kai autos of the following unit, or be supplied with hosautos; it cannot be assigned to one reading.
Same ambiguity: the one 'also' in the ASV clause may render kai autos here or the kai of the preceding unit, so neither the plus nor its absence is shown.
'digged in the earth' is the ordinary English for the accusative oryxen gen as well as for the prepositional en te ge.
'hid' renders ekrypsen and the compound apekrypsen alike.
Word order only; 'after a long time' fixes English order regardless of polyn chronon or chronon polyn.
Word order only; 'maketh a reckoning with them' does not reflect the position of logon relative to met' auton.
ASV reads simply 'I have gained other five talents'; the added ep' autois would have produced 'beside them', which the English lacks.
ASV opens 'His lord said unto him' with no connective, matching ephe; the added de would have been rendered 'And his lord said'.
ASV begins the verse 'And he also that received the two talents came', rendering the de that the alternative omits.
ASV 'he that received the two talents' can carry over the participle idiom from the preceding narrative and render the bare ho ta duo talanta; the English does not require labon.
ASV has 'lo, I have gained other two talents' with no 'beside them'; the added ep' autois is unrendered.
Word order only; 'thou oughtest therefore' places the inferential particle by English convention either way.
ASV 'my money' is a mass noun that renders the plural ta arguria and the singular to argyrion identically.
'from him that hath not' supplies 'from' for the genitive of separation with airo just as it renders an explicit apo; the preposition does not distinguish the readings.
ASV reads 'all the angels with him' with no epithet; the added hagioi would have given 'all the holy angels'.
English 'shall be gathered' is the same form for the plural synachthesontai and the singular synachthesetai with the neuter plural subject.
'sick' renders the participle asthenounta and the adjective asthene alike.
ASV's vocative 'ye cursed' does not show whether the article stood before kateramenoi; the note is an alternative_rendering about the participle's sense, not the article.
ASV joins the clauses asyndetically, 'I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink', with no 'and' before 'I was thirsty'; the reading with kai edipsesa would have been rendered 'and I was thirsty'.
